title: The Hollow of the Sundered Sea
premise: Bram Brightwater, runaway apprentice to a hedge-witch, keeps the ledgers of the Gildenscale, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names sold at auction. When tonight's date surfaces in a century-old book of prophecies, Bram and the guild's ragged found family are pulled into a prophecy that names one of them as the Sunderer, the figure destined to reignite the war between the sea-folk and the shore. As the long winter falls and the prophecy tightens like a net, Bram must choose between loyalty to the people who became their family and the truth that could save—or doom—them all. In the end, Bram rewrites the ledger itself, trading their own remembered past to unmake the prophecy, and the guild survives as something new: keepers of memory rather than merchants of it.
about_author: Ivo Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime trade records before turning to fantasy. They write about ledgers, tides, and the people who fall between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A night of routine inventory at the Gildenscale—bottled fog, a widow's borrowed year—establishes the guild's warmth and its rules. Bram, still hiding from the hedge-witch who raised them, finds comfort in numbers that never lie. Emotional beat: belonging bought with secrecy.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cataloguing a seized estate, Bram opens a century-old prophetic codex and finds tonight's date inked in faded ash-brown script, followed by a line naming 'the keeper of accounts.' The page is warm to the touch. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Gildenscale Gathers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through guild members: Mistress Vael the auctioneer, Osk the tide-reader, Juniper the forger, old Pell the doorkeeper. Each reacts differently to Bram's discovery—dismissal, fear, hunger. The guild votes to investigate. Emotional beat: a family arguing like a family.

chapters.title: What the Tide-Reader Saw
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Reading the harbor at dawn, Osk finds the water pulling backward, toward the drowned ruins of the Sundered Sea. He confesses he has seen this omen once before—in the last winter before the ancient war. Emotional beat: guilt, because he kept it secret.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Names Its Own
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Deciphering the codex with Juniper, Bram learns the prophecy foretells a Sunderer who will reignite the war—and the description matches someone inside the guild. Paranoia blooms over supper. Emotional beat: love curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Letters from the Hedge
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A letter arrives from Maren, the hedge-witch Bram fled three years ago, warning that she too has read the signs and is coming. Flashbacks reveal why Bram ran: Maren wanted to use Bram's rare gift for reading true text. Emotional beat: the past knocking.

chapters.title: The Buyer with Grey Eyes
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. A stranger offers the guild a fortune for the codex—and knows details of the prophecy no outsider should. Vael refuses, but realizes the buyer represents the Remnant, heirs of the sea-folk who want the war refought. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Blood
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The long winter begins early. Guild agents are attacked retrieving a second prophetic fragment; one dies holding a scrap that reads 'the keeper bleeds first.' Pell, oldest of them, remembers the last war's cost. Emotional beat: grief as inheritance.

chapters.title: Juniper's Perfect Forgery
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. To buy time, Juniper forges a false codex to sell the Remnant. It works—but forging prophecy requires believing it, and the act leaves her doubting which memories of her own childhood are real. Emotional beat: identity fraying under craft.

chapters.title: Maren at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The hedge-witch arrives, older and softer than Bram remembered—or so it seems. She offers to help decode the fragment but asks to see Bram's hands, the way she used to before lessons. Bram refuses. Emotional beat: longing and self-protection in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Osk and Bram's shared POV. Guided by the backward tide, they dive the ruins of the Sundered Sea and find the original archive: proof the prophecy was written by the victors, edited to hide who truly broke the peace. Emotional beat: awe giving way to anger at history's authors.

chapters.title: Half a Truth Told
chapters.summary: Guild council scene, Bram's POV. Bram reveals the archive but conceals one detail: the edited line suggests the Sunderer is not a villain but a sacrifice. Bram hides this to protect the family from despair. Emotional beat: the first lie told out of love.

chapters.title: The Remnant Comes to Auction
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. The grey-eyed buyer returns with soldiers, demanding the true codex. Vael stalls with a public auction of worthless wonders while the guild smuggles the archive out through Pell's old smuggler routes. Emotional beat: showmanship as armor.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Salt Cellar
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Someone has sold the route to the Remnant; the smuggled archive is seized and Pell is captured. Evidence points to Juniper—her forged codex was found among the enemy's things. Emotional beat: the found family cracking along its oldest fault lines.

chapters.title: Maren's True Lesson
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Confronting Maren, Bram discovers she did not come to help or to punish: she came because the prophecy's final page names her as the one who must kill the Sunderer. She trained Bram to read true text for this moment. Emotional beat: horror at being shaped for a purpose.

chapters.title: The Keeper Bleeds First
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Ambushed by the Remnant, Bram is wounded protecting the codex and understands at last—the 'keeper of accounts' is themselves, and the prophecy requires the keeper's blood to open the final page. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Juniper's Confession
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Imprisoned by her own family's suspicion, Juniper admits she traded the route—not to the Remnant, but to ransom Pell, believing she alone should bear the risk. Her forged memories were the price the forgery took. Emotional beat: shame met, at last, with forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Last Page of Winter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With Maren's reluctant aid, Bram opens the final page with their blood. The complete prophecy is revealed: the Sunderer must die willingly at midwinter to seal the war away again—and the guild must choose who pays. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: Midwinter at the Sundered Sea
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV converging on the drowned shore. The Remnant forces the ritual early; Maren raises her blade; Osk turns the tide; Vael bargains with the sea-folk's living queen using the truth of the edited archive. Emotional beat: every theme colliding on one frozen beach.

chapters.title: The Ledger Rewritten
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. Instead of dying, Bram does what they do best: they amend the record. Using their gift for true text, Bram strikes the sacrifice clause and enters a new price—their own memories of the hedge, of Maren, of who they were before the guild. Emotional beat: selfhood offered up willingly.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. The war-seal holds; the Remnant kneels to their queen's new treaty; Maren leaves without the apprentice she came for, because Bram no longer remembers needing to run. Osk watches the tide flow forward again. Emotional beat: mourning and relief braided together.

chapters.title: Keepers of Memory
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, resolution. Spring comes late but it comes. The Gildenscale reopens—not trading impossible things, but safeguarding them, with Bram's blank pages where a childhood used to be. Juniper teaches Bram their own story, one evening at a time. Emotional beat: found family chosen twice, once without memory and once with.
